PaletteCycleLoop: Endless loop: PaletteRestart restarts the bundle (ID in animScratch+2 = the spawn parameter), PaletteStep plays it through, BRA restarts it.
PaletteParentChildSpawnWave: Spawns the child (PaletteParentChildWaveLoop) and stores its slot in chatPtr, waits for event flag #01 to clear, kills the child by running KillThinker with X = D = the child slot, then restarts the parent at loc_00B600 (bundle #03 sub-entry 0 and the flag poll).
PaletteParentChildWaveLoop: Child thinker: PaletteStart #03 (load sub-entry 0, yield), PaletteStep (yield until the next sub-entry; falls through at the end of the bundle), BRA back. Runs until the parent kills it when flag #01 clears.
PaletteResetAndKillThinker:
Thinker script body (spawned with COP SpawnThinkerParam, about a dozen callers): COP PaletteRestart, PaletteStep, then KillThinker.

Resets the palette fade machinery for one frame and removes the thinker.
PaletteRestart: COP #36 with no operands. Restarts the bundle whose ID is already in animScratch+2: branches into the shared tail of PaletteStart (loc_009370), which zeroes the sub-entry index, loads and applies sub-entry 0, saves the resume address and yields. It does not set the bundle ID itself (not "bundle 0"): ambient thinkers get it from their spawn parameter, and the 2 sites are ambient_palette_cycler and PaletteResetAndKillThinker (actor_pool).
PaletteStart: COP #37 with one byte operand (palette bundle ID, 84 sites). Stores the ID in animScratch+2, zeroes the sub-entry index ($0E), loads sub-entry 0 with LoadPaletteBundle and applies it with CopyPaletteBundleFrame. Then stores the address after the operand in $00 (the actor entry point) and yields with PLA, PLA, RTL, so the next frame resumes at the following op (normally PaletteStep).
PaletteStartLoop: COP #38 with two byte operands (bundle ID, pass count). Stores the ID in animScratch+2 and the pass count in retPtr1, zeroes the sub-entry index, applies sub-entry 0 and yields exactly like PaletteStart. The count is the TOTAL number of passes PaletteStepLoop makes through the bundle (a count of 0 would give 65,536 passes, by the DEC in StepLoop). Only 3 sites use it: two attack_ability_system effects (#2A/#4B with 2 passes) and one unused script.
PaletteStep: COP #39 with no operands (85 sites). Decrements the frames-left counter in spritesetPtr once per call. While it is still nonzero the counter is stored back, the strip's wait value (animScratch, sub-entry byte 5) is re-seeded into the wait counter $08 and CopyPaletteBundleFrame copies the strip's next frame; then the actor yields (the entry point saved by PaletteStart makes the same Step op run next frame). When the counter reaches zero LoadPaletteBundle loads the next sub-entry: carry clear = another strip, whose first frame is applied before the actor yields; carry set = end of bundle, so the script continues past this op with RTI and the sub-entry index has been reset to 0.
PaletteStepLoop: COP #3A with no operands. Same hold/frame logic as PaletteStep, but when LoadPaletteBundle reports the end of the bundle it decrements the pass counter in retPtr1: if nonzero it is stored and the bundle restarts at once (LoadPaletteBundle already reset the sub-entry index), and only when the counter reaches zero does the script continue with RTI. Pairs with PaletteStartLoop, which sets retPtr1.
ParallaxBuildHdmaTable:
Rewrites the whole HDMA table for the entry chosen by the spawn parameter. Switches D to 0 (restored from the stacked X at every exit) so $00-$26 are global scratch: $00 = record size then stride, $02 = register index, $04 = entry stride, $08 = lines emitted (window path), $0E = lines left in the current band, $10 = lines still to fill (starts at 224), $18 = scroll multiplicand, $1A = camera delta, $1C = vertical position, $20-$26 = window working values, $5E / $60 = table start / bank for the HDMA bind, $62 / $64 = write pointer.
Dispatches on the record size: 4 = ParallaxConstantBandRecords, 9 = ParallaxWindowRecords, anything else (8) = ParallaxScrollBandRecords.
ParallaxClearBandAccumulators: Zeroes the 24 words $0720-$074F that hold the per-band scroll accumulators. Called only at spawn, so accumulators persist (and keep running) across frames. Entries that use more than 24 accumulators (types $05 and $24) are not fully covered.
ParallaxComputeBandValue: Computes one scroll band's value into $06 and its accumulator word. Factor <> 0: accumulator = (factor low byte x $18 / factor high byte) + base, i.e. a proportional follow of the scroll source. Factor = 0: accumulator += base + $1A, an auto-scroll.
ParallaxConstantBandRecords: Constant-band records (size 4). Skips bands above the screen, then ParallaxEmitConstantBands emits the rest.
ParallaxEmitConstantBands: The same loop for constant bands (size 4): value = record word +2 copied unchanged. Used by the COLDATA, CGADSUB and CGDATA entries.
ParallaxEmitScrollBands: Emits scroll bands (size 8) starting at the current record until $10 (lines left) reaches 0 or the list ends. The first band uses only its visible part (-running sum). Each band calls ParallaxComputeBandValue, writes count bytes of at most $7F lines and stores the accumulator >> 4, sign-extended from bit 11, as the value. The band heights it consumes are stored as negative words.
ParallaxEmitWindowRect: Converts one visible rectangle into $24 (first line), $26 (line count) and a WH0/WH1 word (left in the low byte, right in the high byte, right clamped to $FF). A rectangle partly above the screen starts at line 0 with the visible part of its height; one that starts left of the screen gets WH0 = 0.
ParallaxEmitWindowRows: Emits the gap between the previous rectangle and this one (value $0000) and then the rectangle's own lines (the window word in Y). Counts are split into HDMA entries of at most $7F lines and $08 tracks the total. The 3-byte stride is hard-coded.
ParallaxResolveEntryStride: Looks up hdma_channel_config[register index] & 7 (the DMAP transfer mode), then hdma_entry_stride_by_mode[mode] into $04. The result is the byte stride of one HDMA entry (count + data): 2 for mode 0, 3 for modes 1 and 2. It is a stride, not a speed.
ParallaxScrollBandRecords: Scroll-band records (size 8). Walks the records; a band whose running height sum is still non-negative is above the screen and only updates its accumulator (ParallaxComputeBandValue). The first band that crosses into the visible area jumps to ParallaxEmitScrollBands, which emits it and every following band.
ParallaxThinkerEntry: Thinker body. Runs once to clear the accumulators, then loops through SetEntryHere every frame: build the table, bind the channel. See the block note for the entry format.
ParallaxWindowRecords: Window-rectangle records (size 9). Each rectangle is clipped against bg1ScrollH / mapScrollV and, if visible, emitted by ParallaxEmitWindowRect. A negative x word ends the list, after which one final $0000 line and the terminator are written.
ParseMapEntry: Decodes the 3-byte record at stream address X: byte 0 = tile X (bit 7 set = end of stream, carry set), byte 1 = tile Y, byte 2 = metatile ID. Zero-extends (not sign-extends) the coordinates into DP $18/$1C, stores pixel positions (x16) in $1A/$1E and the metatile ID in $00, returns carry clear. Sets D = 0 itself.
ParseSignedTileOffset: Internal JSR helper that reads two signed byte operands from the script pointer at $0A (D = actor slot). Sign-extends each offset, scales by 16 pixels, adds them to the actor position ($14/$16, with Y reduced by $10, one tile row), and converts the result to tile coordinates in $0018/$001C. Returns via RTS with $0A advanced past both operands. Called only by MarkSolidOffset and ClearSolidOffset; BranchIfSolidOffset repeats the arithmetic inline in pixel units.
player_idle_entry_table: Four word entries (50960-50967) indexed by A * 2: IdleStandSouth, IdleStandNorth, IdleStandWest, IdleStandEast (the same order as GetPlayerFacingDirection: 0 down, 1 up, 2 left, 3 right). Read with a long-indexed load; all four handlers share one bank.
PlayerAuraAlignToSolidSouth: Scan down one 16 px row at a time until BranchIfSolidHere reports a blocked tile; the whole scan runs inside one frame.
PlayerAuraBlockedBySolid: Blocked tile found: when the tile below (Y + 16) has terrain type $04 go to PlayerAuraDescendToFloor; otherwise restore the saved position, show frame 1 once and leave through PlayerAuraTransformExit.
PlayerAuraDescendToFloor: Restore the saved X / Y, set $10 bit $2000 and sink: PlayerAuraScanSolidRow.
PlayerAuraLandAnimLoop: One pass of the landing slide: anim 2, +1 px per frame, then test the tile type.
PlayerAuraLandComplete: Open tile reached: clear $10 bit $0002, show frame $1C (anim $1C, no movement) and fall into PlayerAuraTransformExit.
PlayerAuraLandOnSolid: Type $04 reached: clear $2000, set $10 bit $0002 (meaning not traced) and slide down with sprite anim 2 / Y chain 1 (+1 px per frame) until the tile type at the actor is 0.
PlayerAuraScanSolidNext: Sink 1 px and continue next frame (JumpNextFrame).
PlayerAuraScanSolidRow: Every 16th pixel row test for terrain type $04 at the actor position; on a match land.
PlayerAuraTransformEntry: Aura (item_use_system.UseItem_Aura, Shadow standing still): lock the player, leave collision-aware movement, $10 |= $0200, body table index 8, frame 0; save X / Y in $24 / $26, align Y to a 16 px row, then search for floor (PlayerAuraAlignToSolidSouth). The terrain type $04 test below decides between the sink and an abort.
PlayerAuraTransformExit: End: normal movement again ($10 |= $0008, clear $0200), no pending wait, PlayerIdleEntry (clears the $0800 lock).
PlayerFallFromHeight: Fall into the scene (awBD_fall_trigger): hide the buttons, lock the player, leave collision-aware movement, freeze the camera; 4 ticks (WaitByte #03) out of the depth sort, Y -= 128, then 8 passes of fall anim $19 with Y chain 7 (+4 px per frame), landing SFX $2C and frame $1C. Then restore $10 / camera / buttons and return to PlayerIdleEntry (which clears the $0800 lock). Whether the fall ends exactly on the original Y is not checked.
PlayerIdleAnimContinue: Loop: SetEntryHere, AnimOnce, repeat. Each pass saves the loop as the re-entry point and plays the animation once.
PlayerIdleAnimLoop: Entered as the player's script. When per-scene flag #00 is set it stages anim $11 (PlayerIdleUseShadowSprite), otherwise anim $01, then loops AnimOnce until the caller redirects the player. What flag #00 means is not traced.
PlayerIdleUseShadowSprite: Per-scene flag #00 set: stage anim $11 instead of $01.
PlayerPoseHold: Hold pose: body table index 4, then every frame stage frame $20 and play it once (SetEntryHere + RTL). The callers place the player first (gs2E_sleep also moves it up 8 px).
PlayerPoseHoldExit: Leave the held pose: body 4 frame $20 once, then PlayerIdleEntry.
PlayerSkyGardenJumpLanding: Jump sequence of sg4D_jump_handler (the caller sets playerFlags $0800): leave collision-aware movement, $10 |= $2200, Y -= 64, freeze the camera, 4 ticks (WaitByte #03), Y += 64, show the player, flip the sprite vertically, Y -= 32 and rise with decelerating Y chains (8 x4 passes, 4 x2, 2 x2); flip back, Y += 32, descend (chains 1, 3), landing SFX $2C and frame $1F; restore $10 and the camera and return to PlayerIdleEntry. The buttons are not masked or unmasked here.
PlayerStaticBodyAnimLoop: Stage frame $1F and play it once, forever.
PlayerStaticBodyPose: Flute pose: $10 |= $0200, body table index 4 (SetPlayerSpriteDirect), then frame $1F is staged again on every pass. item_use_system writes this as the player's script while the melody plays.
PlayerWalkingIdlePose: End of the flute: clear $10 bit $0200 and fall into RestorePlayerControlDirect.
PlaySoundBoth: COP #08 with one word operand (two SFX bytes packed). Stores the entire 16-bit value to sfxQueueCh1 as a word, filling both $06F8 and $06F9 in one write.
PlaySoundCh1: COP #07 with one byte operand (SFX ID). Writes the byte directly to sfxQueueCh1 ($06F8) for channel-1 sound effect playback.
PlaySoundCh2: COP #06 with one byte operand (SFX ID). Writes the byte directly to sfxQueueCh2 ($06F9) for channel-2 sound effect playback.
PrintDialogString:
COP #BF with one word operand (text pointer).

Sets displayModeFlags bit 13 ($2000; no reader found), calls UpdateFrameRender to sync the display, clears actor $10 bit 11 and joypadMaskStd, renders the text via DialogStringRenderer, then restores the mask, re-applies it to joypadCurrent (TRB) and clears the D-pad bits ($0F00) in joypadHeld.
PrintDialogStringAlt:
COP #6B with one word operand (text pointer).

Like PrintDialogString but without the bit 13 set/clear and the UpdateFrameRender sync, and it does not re-apply the mask to joypadCurrent; it still clears actor $10 bit 11 and joypadMaskStd while rendering and clears the D-pad bits in joypadHeld afterwards.
ProcessAnimFlag:
Internal JSR helper shared by all StageSprite* ops. Clears the frame counter $2A, then interprets the animation index byte in A:
- $FF: keep $28 unchanged and return (the flip bit is not touched either).
- bit 7 set: $28 = low 7 bits; unless $12 bit 1 is set, set the horizontal flip $4000 in the OAM attribute word $0E (the mirrored variant of the animation).
- otherwise: $28 = the byte; unless $12 bit 1 is set, clear the flip bit.
$12 bit 1 therefore acts as a mirror lock that freezes the flip state across later Stage ops. Returns with RTS.
push_handler_forceball: Force-ball variant: also needs the matching player pose ($28 = $3A..$3D) and mirrors the parent position while idle.
push_handler_solid: Idle loop for a pullable solid: same arm / poll / gate preamble as the gem handler.
PushForceballDistPlayerNorth: Minimum-distance check ($20) in PushForceballMovePlayerNorth before sprite and facing tests.
PushForceballDistPlayerWest: Minimum-distance check ($20) in PushForceballMovePlayerWest before sprite and facing tests.
PushForceballMovePlayerEast: East-side forceball pull with sprIdx $3C, facing left, X nudge +$10.
PushForceballMovePlayerNorth: Forceball pull when the player is above: distance and sprIdx $3A checks, facing down, NudgePosition (0,-$10), sound $2C, 16-step parent Y slide; south/west/east halves mirror with other facings and offsets.
PushForceballMovePlayerSouth: South half of forceball vertical pull: sprIdx $3B, facing up, nudge Y+$10, slide loop toward player.
PushForceballMovePlayerWest: West-side forceball pull with sprIdx $3D, facing right, X nudge -$10.
PushForceballRestorePlayerNorth: RestoreSavedPtr exit for the north-side forceball pull.
PushForceballRestorePlayerSouth: RestoreSavedPtr for south forceball pull failures or completion.
PushSolidCheckState: Skips this frame (RTL) while the parent has $10 bit $0080 (iframe-active per combat_collision) and does not carry $12 bit $0010.
PushSolidClearPushingFlag: Parent $12 = ($12 and $FFEF) or the saved bit in $24, i.e. restore the state from before the slide.
PushSolidDistPlayerNorth: Distance gate in the north-side solid pull path after abs Y delta: compares to $20 and branches to PushSolidRestorePlayerNorth when the player is too close; otherwise checks facing and collision.
PushSolidDistPlayerWest: Distance gate in the west-side solid pull path after abs X delta: same $20 minimum before facing and tile tests.
PushSolidMovePlayerEast: Player east of the solid: facing 2 (left), tile one column east free; the solid moves east one tile.
PushSolidMovePlayerNorth: Same-column block (player above or below the solid): needs |posY delta| >= $20, facing 0 (down), tile one row up free; the solid moves up one tile.
PushSolidMovePlayerSouth: Player below the solid: facing 1 (up), tile one row down free; the solid moves down one tile.
PushSolidMovePlayerWest: Same-row block (player west or east): needs |posX delta| >= $20, facing 3 (right), tile one column west free; the solid moves west one tile.
PushSolidRestorePlayerEast: RestoreSavedPtr exit for the east-side solid pull.
PushSolidRestorePlayerNorth: Idle restore for the north-side solid pull path: COP RestoreSavedPtr only.
PushSolidRestorePlayerSouth: RestoreSavedPtr exit for the south-side solid pull.
PushSolidRestorePlayerWest: RestoreSavedPtr exit for the west-side solid pull.
PushSolidSetPushingFlag: Parent $12 |= $0010 for the slide. The previous value of that bit goes to $24 (this handler's scratch); returns with RTS.
QueueHdma: COP #01 (18 sites). Operands: a 3-byte table address (word + bank, e.g. $7E8800 or @label) and a byte naming the PPU B-bus register ($21xx, e.g. #0F = BG2HOFS). The handler reads them as two words: Y = address, A = bank (low byte) | register (high byte). SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect then picks the DMAP transfer mode from hdma_channel_config[register], ORs $40 (indirect addressing), uses the bank for both the table and the indirect data, and binds the NEXT free channel (allocated from channel 1 upward via $68/$6A; reset by ResetHdmaState). The channel is armed through the HDMA enable mask ($66).
QueueHdmaChannel: COP #03 (2 sites, both in scene_lifecycle: channels 6 and 7 for the BG1/BG2 horizontal scroll window). Operands: a byte channel number (0–7), a 3-byte table address, and a byte B-bus register. Unlike #01/#02 it programs the named channel directly: register block offset = channel × 16 ($4300 + offset), channel bit ORed into the HDMA enable mask $66, DMAP = hdma_channel_config[register] | $40 (indirect), DASB = A1B = bank, BBAD = register, A1T = table address. The handler PHYs the slot and PLXes it back at the end instead of using TYX, and uses WRAM $0000/$0002 as scratch.
QueueHdmaDirect: COP #02 (28 sites). Same operands as QueueHdma (3-byte table address, B-bus register byte; used for window position registers #26, mode 7 matrix registers #1B–#1E, scroll registers and others). It calls SetupHdmaChannel_Direct, which writes DMAP WITHOUT the $40 flag and still sets the channel's bit in the HDMA enable mask, so this is a DIRECT-table HDMA channel (each table entry holds the register data inline), not a general linear DMA transfer. The name QueueHdmaDirect is misleading; QueueHdma is the indirect variant.
QueueMapChange:
COP #26 with one byte (scene ID), two words (spawn X, Y), one byte (flags) and one word (scroll parameters). Writes sceneNext ($0642), warpDestX/Y ($064C/$064E), warpFacing ($0650, the flags byte) and warpScrollParams ($0652).

If flags bit 7 is set it is cleared in warpFacing and the address of this operand block (PC − 8) and its bank are stored in sceneSaveData and reviveWarpPtr. The operand block has the layout of a warp record (entry+4 in the warp table), and game_over_sequence reloads from these pointers, so bit 7 marks the scene change as the new revive/save point; nothing resumes at that address as script code.
ramp_motion_curve_step: One frame of the arc: read the next signed byte of the curve (orbitAngle + frame index $2A), sign-extend and add it to the player's Y at $16. LoopEnd repeats it once per frame for the curve's frame count.
RampArcDriver: Arc driver child of the east/west climbs. X = $04 link = the player. Selects the curve from the player's statsPtr, sets loopCounter = frame count and orbitAngle = byte offset of the curve, then runs ramp_motion_curve_step once per frame. At the end: playerSpeedEw = orbitDiameter (exit speed), RestorePlayerControl, step counters reset, COP Die.
RampBeginPlayerControl: Takes the player over: zero both speeds, statsPtr = ramp $0E (curve index or loop count), zero player $2C / $2E, mask the D-pad ($0F00) and set playerFlags $0800. Y = player actor on entry; X = the ramp.
RampCheckPlayerSpeed: A = signed speed on the ramp's axis. Carry clear = |speed| >= 6 and playerFlags $0800 clear; carry set otherwise.
RampClimbNorthStep: Loop head of the NORTH climb: animation $1E, Y chain $10 (-8 per frame), one animation cycle per iteration; after the last iteration playerSpeedNs = $FFF8 and control is restored.
RampClimbSouthStep: Loop head of the SOUTH climb: animation $19, Y chain $0F (+8 per frame), one animation cycle per iteration; after the last iteration playerSpeedNs = $0008 and control is restored.
RampEastArmed: ramp_east stage 2: SetEntryHere again, then compare player X with ramp X each frame. Equal: RampEastLaunch launches. Distance >= $10: back to stage 1. Otherwise keep waiting.
RampEastLaunch: ramp_east launch: point the player's entry at RampPlayerClimbEast, run RampBeginPlayerControl, return to stage 1.
RampEastWatch: ramp_east stage 1 (re-entered by JumpNextFrame). Scratch $0018 = ramp X + 8, then the speed, row (|dy| <= $18) and column (player X - ramp X in 2..15) checks. RTL leaves the ramp at this entry for the next frame.
RampNorthArmed: ramp_north stage 2: compare player Y with ramp Y each frame.
RampNorthLaunch: ramp_north launch: the player's entry becomes RampPlayerClimbNorth (the north climb).
RampNorthWatch: ramp_north stage 1: axis Y. Checks playerSpeedNs, |player X - ramp X| <= $10 and player Y - ramp Y in 2..15.
RampPlayerClimbEast: East-ramp climb (runs as the player): spawn the arc child, give it the exit speed $FFF8, then loop animation $21 with X chain $10 (-8 per frame) until the child restores control.
RampPlayerClimbNorth: North-ramp climb entry: loopCounter = statsPtr, loop head RampClimbNorthStep. Clears $0008 / sets $0200 in the player's $10.
RampPlayerClimbSouth: South-ramp climb entry: loopCounter = statsPtr, loop head RampClimbSouthStep, SetEntryHere, clears $0008 / sets $0200 in the player's $10.
RampPlayerClimbWest: West-ramp climb (unnamed in the original): same as RampPlayerClimbEast with exit speed $0008, animation $24 and X chain $0F (+8 per frame).
RampSouthArmed: ramp_south stage 2: compare player Y with ramp Y each frame.
RampSouthLaunch: ramp_south launch: the player's entry becomes RampPlayerClimbSouth.
RampSouthWatch: ramp_south stage 1: scratch $001C = ramp Y - $10; the window is player Y - ramp Y in -16..-2 with |dx| <= $10.
RampWestLaunch: ramp_west launch: the player's entry becomes RampPlayerClimbWest (the west climb).
RampWestWatch: ramp_west stage 1. Scratch $0018 = ramp X - 8; the window is player X - ramp X in -16..-2.
ReadDirSprite_XVelocity: Same as ReadDirSprite_YVelocity, but the velocity-curve pointer goes to $2C (X axis) instead of $2E.
ReadDirSprite_YVelocity:
Read the next walk-step stream byte and set up the sprite and the Y velocity curve for it.

Y = stream pointer (warpFacing, $0650), incremented by one. The byte indexes walk_step_table (word entries): the whole word goes to $0000 (low byte = animation index used by StagePlayerSprFromDP); its high byte indexes move_chain_table, and that pointer (head of a delta-node velocity list) is stored in $2E. ReadDirSprite_XVelocity is identical but stores it in $2C.
ReadDivideResult: Hardware divide latency wrapper. Five NOPs provide the 16-cycle wait required after writing WRDIVB before the SNES hardware divider result is valid, then reads RDDIVL into A. Called by MultiplyThenDivide.
ReadMultiplyResult: Hardware multiply latency wrapper. One NOP provides the 8-cycle wait required after writing WRMPYB before the SNES hardware multiplier result is valid, then reads RDMPYL into Y. Called by MultiplyThenDivide.
ReloadMoveChains: COP #B1 with no operands. Re-runs AnimFrameLookup for the current moveXAlt and moveYAlt and stores the chain pointers in $2C and $2E again, rewinding both chains to their first node.
RemoveItem: COP #D5 with one byte operand (item ID). Calls RemoveItemFromInventory (zeroes the matching slot and, as a side effect, resets the equipped state: inventoryEquippedType = 0, inventoryEquippedIndex = $FFFF) and continues.
ResetVector: CPU reset entry point. Disables interrupts, clears carry, switches from 65816 emulation mode to native mode via XCE, then jumps long to SystemInit.
ResolveActorIndex: Internal JSR helper that converts an 8-bit actor list index in A to a WRAM actor pointer in Y. Computes Y = index × $30 + $1000 using Multiply8x8Unsigned, matching the fixed $30-byte actor structure layout. Called by BranchIfActorNear and BranchIfActorAt before distance or coordinate comparisons.
ResolveFacingFromAxisBase:
Picks the desired facing frame and turns toward it. Desired = ($0000 base + offset) & 15, where the offset comes from the slope row in orbitAngle: row ≥ $0D → 0, $05-$0C → 1, < 5 → 2; ResolveFacingFromDiagonalBase (next block) swaps offsets 0 and 2.

The shared tail (sub-labels in the Alt block) then compares it with animScratch2 (the current facing, 16 frames clockwise from north): $FFFF (unset) or within one frame snaps to the desired frame and sets $0000 = $FFFF (aligned); otherwise the facing moves one frame the short way round (a half-turn counts as counter-clockwise). Unless chatPtr bit 15 is set, the spawner's animation becomes chatPtr + facing ($28, frame counter $2A = 0) and UpdateActorAnimation is run for it. Finally it jumps through FollowDirectionTable to the FollowDirHandler for the new facing, with carry = chatPtr bit 15.
ResolveFacingFromDiagonalBase: Alt entry of ResolveFacingFromAxisBase with offsets 0 and 2 swapped (row ≥ $0D → 2, < 5 → 0). The normal entry is used by the handlers whose base frame is an axis frame (N, E, S, W: axis-aligned row = base), the Alt entry by those whose base is a diagonal frame (NE, SE, SW, NW: axis-aligned row = base + 2). The labels ResolveFacingOffset0/Diagonal/MoveYOnly describe the normal entry only.
ResolveTileData: Writes one metatile of layer 0: map index from TileCoordsToMapIndex (layer selector 0), collision byte from $7F0000 + ID copied to $7FC000 + index, the ID to mapLayerTilemap ($7EA000 + index). If the tile is inside the visible window it then copies the four tile words of the definition at $7E2000 + ID x 8 to $0904/$0906/$090A/$090C and stores the VRAM word addresses of the two tile rows in $0902 and $0908 (PixelToVramAddress, BG1 nametable). Off-screen tiles stop after the map writes.
RestorePlayerControl: Returns the player to normal locomotion: entry pointer = PlayerIdleEntry, $2C/$2E/$08 zeroed, $10 = ($10 and $FDFF) or $0008, D-pad un-masked ($0F00 from joypadMaskStd), playerFlags $0800 cleared. Called from UnlockPlayerAfterClimb and from three ramp exits in ramps.asm.
RestoreSavedPtr: COP #C5 with no operands. If retPtr1 ($7F0004) is non-zero, restores it as the script PC and clears retPtr1; otherwise yields via RTL.
ResumeAfterSnap: COP #4A with no operands. Restores the saved script PC and bank from snapResumePtr ($7F1018) and $7F101A after grid snapping completes, then clears both save slots.
ReturnActorSlot:
Push actor slot X back on the free list and decrement the counters (JSR; D must equal X).

Zeroes D so the free-list pointer ($4E) can be used as [$4E], backs the pointer up by 2 with an 8-bit DEC (no borrow; safe because the whole list sits inside page $0E), decrements activeActorCount, stores X into the freed entry and finally sets D = X again, undoing its own TCD #0.
ReturnWithSignal: COP #E1 with no operands. Restores the deferred call PC from retPtr1 (clearing it); if set, RTI-resumes with A=$FFFF as a non-zero signal to the caller, otherwise yields via RTL.
RewardDefPickup: Tier 3 or more: spawn e_def_increase (flags $1000, $12 $1000) and Die.
RewardNone: No reward: drop the pushed tier and Die.
RngByte:
COP #23 with no operands. Steps a 16-byte additive generator over $0410–$041F and returns the new $0410 byte in A.

For X = 15..1: byte[$040F+X] += byte[$0410+X] + carry (one carry chain, so $041E += $041F first and $0410 += $0411 last). Then a ripple counter at $041F is incremented, carrying toward lower addresses. rngState ($040F) is the index base; $040F itself is never touched.
RngMod:
COP #24 with one byte operand (modulus). Reduces the current RngByte output ($0410) by repeated subtraction and stores the remainder in rngModuloResult ($0420). Does not advance the generator.

A modulus of 0 would loop forever (the subtraction never goes negative); extracted/ uses $50 and $60.
RunBg3Script:
COP #BD BG3 console-script runner taking one Address operand: a far pointer to a BG3 tilemap command stream.

Switches the data bank, calls ConsoleStringRenderer with the direct page zeroed, then sets displayModeFlags bit 0 (full BG3 staging-buffer upload request). Used by the diary menu, title screen and boot-logo actors, and by UpdateHUD for the HUD counters.
RunPlayerAnim: COP #93 with no operands, identical to AnimOnce (#89): one UpdateActorAnimation pass; yields (PLA PLA RTL) while the animation runs, and on completion zeroes $2C/$2E and continues. 8 sites.
ScrollCameraAccumulate:
Accumulative camera scroll actor-def used in Pyramid interior scenes.

Zeroes the accumulators at DP $24 (X) and $26 (Y), packs the position via TileAlignPosition, then each frame calls ComputeScrollDeltas and adds the accumulators to cameraDeltaX and cameraDeltaY. Other actors can write $24/$26 to add drift on top of the standard tracking.
ScrollCameraInit:
Camera initialization scroll actor (spawn #DF, #DF; Mt. Kress scenes).

Sets bit 12 ($1000) in the actor status word, subtracts 8 px (X) and 16 px (Y) from the position parameters and packs both with TileAlignCoord into the multiplier/divisor words $14/$16.

Runs COP LoopStart with count 3 around ComputeScrollDeltas; all three passes use the same inputs, so they give the same result. After the loop, copies cameraDeltaY to effectScrollV ($0690).

Then sets the re-entry point (COP SetEntryHere), computes the deltas again each frame, ORs bit 15 into cameraDeltaX and stores it in forcedScrollOverride ($06C8), and zeroes cameraDeltaX. Outside layer1_scroll_actors no reader of $06C8 was found in extracted/.
ScrollCameraTrack:
Simple continuous camera tracking actor.

Sets bit 12 of the status word, packs the spawn position via TileAlignPosition, then re-runs ComputeScrollDeltas every frame (after COP SetEntryHere) with the current camera targets.

The default camera actor: about 100 scene spawns use it (87 of them with #11, #11).
ScrollCameraVertical:
Vertical-only camera tracking actor-def referenced from scene_actors in Edward's Castle, Itory, Incan Ruins and Dao.

Sets bit 12, packs the position via TileAlignPosition, then every frame computes only the Y delta through MulDivide when $16 is nonzero. cameraDeltaX is left unchanged and the X parameter ($14) is ignored. Three of its spawns use #21, #00, whose Y parameter is 0, so they compute nothing.
SelectFallbackDirection: Entered while the facing is still turning ($0000 not yet $FFFF). A = heading 1-8 stored in $0000 by the FollowDirHandler; (A − 1) & 7 indexes follow_fallback_table, whose entries are the apply halves of the eight octant handlers (headings N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW), so the actor keeps moving along its current facing with the slope row the handler set.
SetActorBody:
Apply the current characterForm's body_table entry to actor X (JSR helper).

Index = form × 6 (each body_table entry is 6 bytes). Writes the spriteset pointer ($7F0006) and bank ($7F0008), then clears playerFlags bit $8000, the sprite-override flag (set by SetPlayerSpriteDirect, see GetPlayerFacingDirection).
SetCollideCallback: COP #5A with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in onCollideCallback ($7F1008) for collision-event dispatch.
SetCollisionAbs: COP #42 (legacy name SetSolidAbs) absolute collision writer taking three byte operands: tile X, tile Y, and a full collision-layer byte value. Converts the tile coordinates through TileCoordsToMapIndex and stores the byte directly into collisionLayer, replacing both nibbles (solid and type) in one write. Used once in the game. The handler has no TYX: it pushes Y (the slot) at entry and recovers it with PLX at the end, after X has been used for the map index.
SetCustomCallback: COP #5E with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in the custom-callback word ($7F1016, written as scratch1010+6) of the actor's slot. combat_collision runs it as the interaction handler for push hits; some actors reuse the word for other data.
SetDeathCallback: COP #57 with an @Code far-pointer operand (word + bank byte, 3 bytes). Stores the word in onDeathCallback ($7F1004) and the bank in the following word ($7F1006), both indexed by actor slot, for the death script hook.
SetDodgeCallback: COP #59 with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in onDodgeCallback ($7F1002) for dodge-event dispatch.
SetDungeonKillFlag: COP #D8 with no script operands. Reads the actor's enemyNum ($7F:0022,X — the dungeon enemy number used for kill tracking) as a flag index and, when its low byte is non-zero, calls SetWramFlag to set that bit in the wramFlags bitfield ($0A80), recording the kill (cleared only as described in flag_helpers). Index 0 is ignored.
SetEntryFar: COP #E2 with one Address operand (word + bank). Writes the far entry pointer to $00/$02 and zeroes $08, then RTI-continues in the current stream without yielding. Unlike JumpFar it does not jump: the new entry only takes effect the next time the actor resumes.
SetEntryHere: COP #C1 with no operands. Saves the current script bank ($0C→$02) and PC ($0A→$00) as the actor entry/resume pointer without yielding.
SetEntryHereAndYield: COP #C2 with no operands. Same entry-pointer save as SetEntryHere, then pops the return address and yields via RTL so execution resumes next frame.
SetEventFlag: Core JSR routine that sets one bit in the eventFlags ($0A00) bitfield. Decomposes the flag index into byte (÷8) and bit (AND $07) indices, ORs the bitmasks_bit_position entry into the eventFlags byte. Called by all SetFlag COP handlers and JSL offset wrappers.
SetEventFlag_0200: JSL helper that sets persistent event flag $0200 + A (bytes $0A40–$0A5F) via SetEventFlag. A is not masked, so callers must pass a 0–$FF index. Callers: warps_interaction (chest opened) and hidden_red_jewel.
SetFlag_0100: JSL helper that sets event/trigger flag $0100 + (A AND $FF), bytes $0A20–$0A3F (callers: StandardEnemyDefeatHandler, EnemyDefeatDispatch, wall walker, mystic ball).
SetFlag_0300: JSL helper that sets event flag $0300 + (A AND $FF); used to mark a scene's clear reward as claimed (reward_actors, boss_clear_reward_handler).
SetFlagByte: COP #CC with one byte operand (flag index). Calls SetEventFlag to OR the corresponding bit in the eventFlags ($0A00) bitfield.
SetFlagRaw: JSL helper that sets an event flag without adding a base offset. Masks to byte and calls SetEventFlag directly.
SetFlagWord: COP #CD with one word operand (flag index). Calls SetEventFlag with the 16-bit flag number.
SetHitCallback: COP #58 with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in onHitCallback ($7F1000) for hit-event dispatch.
SetHMirror: COP #BB with no operands. Sets horizontal mirror bit $4000 on OAM attribute word $0E via TSB.
SetInteractHandler: COP #C0 with one &Code operand. Stores it in the actor's chatPtr ($7F000A), the routine the interaction system runs when the player talks to or touches the actor. Used by NPCs, chests and inspectable objects (322 uses). The copdef name is SetInteractHandler.
SetLinkedEntryPtr:
COP $6A (SetLinkedEntryPtr) with one &Code operand: point the next-linked actor ($06) at a new script.

Only the 16-bit word at the linked actor's $00/$01 is replaced (the 2-byte operand is a same-bank pointer; its bank byte $02 is left as it was), and its waitCounter ($08) and moveX/moveY ($2C/$2E) are zeroed so the new script starts on the linked actor's next tick with no pending wait or velocity. The caller's script pointer is advanced past the operand and the COP returns via RTI, so the caller continues immediately.

Y = linked actor's DP base; $0000,Y works as that actor's DP because DBR=$81 mirrors low WRAM.
SetMetasprite: COP #88 with one word plus one byte operand (186 sites). Sets spritesetPtr ($7F0006) to the word and the spriteset bank ($7F0008) to the byte: the actor's table of frame lists (one list per animation index), not a single metasprite. The next Stage* op selects the list. Does not touch $00/$02 and continues with RTI.
SetMoveNegateX: COP #AD with one byte operand (nonzero sets, zero clears). TSB or TRB bit $4000 on actor flags $12: while set, ApplyMovement and the collision-checked move negate the actor's X delta (the copdef name says SW; the effect is an X flip).
SetMoveNegateXY: COP #AF with one byte operand (nonzero sets, zero clears). TSB or TRB bits $6000 on actor flags $12: negates both the X and Y deltas (reverses the staged movement).
SetMoveNegateY: COP #AE with one byte operand (nonzero sets, zero clears). TSB or TRB bit $2000 on actor flags $12: while set, the Y delta is negated (the copdef name says NE; the effect is a Y flip).
SetPlayerIdleFacing: Sets the player actor's script entry to IdleStandSouth / North / West / East chosen by A (0..3), resets the wait counter and the movement scratch words, and returns with RTL. See the block note.
SetPlayerSpriteDirect: COP #8E with one byte operand (body_table index 0-8). Writes spritesetPtr ($7F0006) and the bank byte ($7F0008) from the 6-byte body_table entry, caches index x 6 in animScratch2 ($7F000E) and the raw index in $0AC8, and sets playerFlags $8000. Does not touch the animation index or frame counter. 24 sites (the Psycho Slider code uses #04 = spriteset_will_abilities).
SetPriorityMax: COP #B2 with no operands. Sets bit $0002 on actor+$10 via TSB: SortActorsByDepth then gives the actor key $0000 (first OAM index), so it draws in front of every other actor.
SetPriorityMin: COP #B3 with no operands. Sets bit $0001 on actor+$10 via TSB: SortActorsByDepth then gives the actor key $01FE (last OAM index), so it draws behind every other actor unless SetPriorityMax is also set.
SetSavedPtr: COP #C6 with one &Code operand. Stores the operand offset as a deferred-return pointer in retPtr1 ($7F0004) for later RestoreSavedPtr/ReturnWithSignal use.
SetScratchPointer: COP #54 with one word plus one byte operand. Stores the far pointer in animScratch ($7F0000 word, $7F0002 bank) for later use by handler or callback code.
SetSpritePalette: COP #B7 with one byte operand (0–7). Clears palette bits $0E00 in $0E, then XBA/TSB to set the 4-bit OAM palette subfield.
SetSpritePriority: COP #B6 with one byte operand (0–3). Clears OAM priority bits $3000 in attribute word $0E, then XBA/TSB to pack the value into the high byte.
SetTilePos: COP #25 with two byte operands (tile X, tile Y). Converts tile coordinates to pixel positions by shifting each ×16; adds 8 to X for horizontal tile-centering and stores results in actor $14/$16.
SetTileStreamAnim: COP #55 with one byte and one word operand (4 sites, all tile-streaming effect actors). Stores the byte in $28 (animation index), clears the frame counter $2A, stores the word in $24 (the VRAM word address AdvanceSpriteAnim streams tiles to; it is copied to $B0) and saves the address after the op in $00 (normally the AdvanceSpriteAnim op) before RTI. Despite the name it resets no sprite state of the composition system.
SetWramFlag: Core JSR routine that sets one bit in the wramFlags ($0A80) bitfield. Decomposes the flag index: byte = index÷8 (LSR×3), bit = index AND $07, then ORs the corresponding bitmasks_bit_position entry into the wramFlags byte. Called by SetDungeonKillFlag and all SetWramFlag JSL wrappers.
SetWramFlag_Offset100: JSL helper that sets wramFlags bit $0100 + (A AND 7) (byte $0AA0, event flags $0500–$0507). Pairs with TestWramFlag_Offset100; the only caller is boss_clear_reward_handler, which marks a boss as rewarded.
sine_hdma_slow_wave: Thinker script: amplitude 8, InitSineHdma, yield; each later frame: wait for event flag $FF (re-initialise while it is clear), TickSineHdma, BindSineHdma, RTL.
SineWaveInit: Init label: set the amplitude ($7F0008,X = 8) and build the four sine tables at $7E8800 (period 64); reached on the first frame and again whenever the flag test finds event flag $FF clear.
SliderGlideEast: Player-side glide for an east slide: X +4 per frame; finish frame $17.
SliderGlideNorth: Player-side glide for a north slide: Y -4 per frame (up the screen); finish frame $11.
SliderGlideSouth: Player-side glide for a south slide: Y +4 per frame (down the screen); finish frame $0E.
SliderGlideTriggerEast: Glide trigger for an EAST-moving Psycho Slide (player animation $15/$16). Needs player X == trigger X and player Y in the window trigger Y - 7 .. trigger Y + $18. On success the player is sent to SliderGlideEast (X +4 per frame). 1 spawn site.
SliderGlideTriggerNorth: Glide trigger for a NORTH-moving Psycho Slide (player animation $0F/$10). Needs player Y == trigger Y exactly and player X in the window trigger X - 7 .. trigger X + $18. Starts with SetEntryHere so the check repeats every frame. On success the player is sent to SliderGlideNorth (Y -4 per frame). 12 spawn sites (plus the awB2 JumpFar into SliderGlideTriggerNorthMain).
SliderGlideTriggerNorthEntry: Entry variant of SliderGlideTriggerNorth: shifts the trigger itself by (-8, 0) pixels once (NudgePosition on the trigger's own slot), then continues into SliderGlideTriggerNorthMain. 1 spawn site.
SliderGlideTriggerNorthMain: Main per-frame entry of SliderGlideTriggerNorth after SetEntryHere: requires the player in a 32 px X window (trigger X minus 8 through plus $18), Y equal to trigger Y, Psycho Slide sprite bank, and animation $0F or $10, then redirects the player to SliderGlideNorth and calls LockPlayerForClimb; otherwise returns with RTL.
SliderGlideTriggerNorthOffset: Entry variant in SliderGlideTriggerNorthEntry: COP NudgePosition shifts the trigger actor by (-8, 0) once, then BRA into SliderGlideTriggerNorthMain for the normal north-slide gate.
SliderGlideTriggerSouth: Glide trigger for a SOUTH-moving Psycho Slide (player animation $0C/$0D). Needs player Y == trigger Y exactly and player X in the window trigger X - 7 .. trigger X + $18. On success the player is sent to SliderGlideSouth (Y +4 per frame). 14 spawn sites, the most used trigger.
SliderGlideTriggerWest: Glide trigger for a WEST-moving Psycho Slide (player animation $12/$13). Needs player X == trigger X exactly and player Y inside the 32-px window trigger Y - 7 .. trigger Y + $18, sprite bank $8F. On success the player is sent to SliderGlideWest (X -4 per frame) and locked by LockPlayerForClimb. 1 spawn site.
SliderGlideWest: Player-side glide for a west slide: entry flags once ($10 |= $2200, bit $0008 cleared), then X -4 per frame while the statsPtr countdown runs; at 0 it leaves script-driven mode, stages the west slide's finish frame $14 and calls UnlockPlayerAfterClimb.
smooth_follow_child: Projectile body. Clears word $2A, spawns SmoothFollowChildTick as a hidden marked child (flags $2000) and hands it the target from $24 (set by the caller: the player). Y = $1FC0 (no free actor) kills the body. Otherwise it plays AnimOnce each frame and dies when its own $10 bit $4000 (off-screen flag) is set. The body never moves by itself: the tick writes its X/Y.
SmoothFollowApplyENE: Heading ENE (target north-east, |dx| > |dy|). Aims once with ComputeFollowAngleAlt, then each frame X += major and Y -= minor.
SmoothFollowApplyESE: Heading ESE (target south-east, |dx| > |dy|). Aims once with ComputeFollowAngleAlt, then each frame X += major and Y += minor.
SmoothFollowApplyNNE: Heading NNE (target north-east, |dy| >= |dx|). Aims once with ComputeFollowAngle, SetEntryHere, then each frame Y -= major ($0000) and X += minor ($0002); writes the position to the body.
SmoothFollowApplyNNW: Heading NNW: target north-west with |dy| >= |dx|. ComputeFollowAngle once, then each frame Y -= major and X -= minor.
SmoothFollowApplySSE: Heading SSE: target south-east (dx >= 0, dy >= 0) with |dy| >= |dx|. ComputeFollowAngle once, then each frame Y += major ($0000) and X += minor ($0002).
SmoothFollowApplySSW: Heading SSW: target south-west (dx < 0, dy >= 0) with |dy| >= |dx|. ComputeFollowAngle once, then each frame Y += major and X -= minor. Reached from the west half of the tick.
SmoothFollowApplyWNW: Heading WNW: target north-west with |dx| > |dy|. ComputeFollowAngleAlt once, then each frame X -= major and Y -= minor.
SmoothFollowApplyWSW: Heading WSW: target south-west with |dx| > |dy|. ComputeFollowAngleAlt once, then each frame X -= major and Y += minor.
SmoothFollowChildBodyLoop: Idle loop of the body: SetEntryHere + AnimOnce (one frame per pass); leaves to SmoothFollowChildDie when the actor box is off-screen ($10 bit $4000).
SmoothFollowChildDie: COP Die. Also the default onCollideCallback: RunInteractionCollision points an actor with extendedFlags $0010 and no callback at this label when it touches the player, so a projectile that hits dies here (after the damage). Die also kills the marked tick child.
SmoothFollowChildTick: Hidden aiming child (spawned by smooth_follow_child, gw8A_sand_fanger and pyDD_mummy_queen). On its first frame: copy the speed from the parent's loopCounter, form dx = target.X - self.X and dy = target.Y - 8 - self.Y (the 8 aims at the target's middle), store |dx| in $0018 and |dy| in $001C and branch to one of 8 handlers by the signs and the larger magnitude (heading table in the block note). The handlers call SetEntryHere after the aim, so this dispatch code runs only once.
SmoothFollowTickGoESE: dx >= 0, dy >= 0, |dy| < |dx|: X-dominant, continue at SmoothFollowApplyESE (ESE).
SmoothFollowTickTargetNorth: dx >= 0, dy < 0 (target north): negate dy, then |dy| >= |dx| goes to SmoothFollowApplyNNE (NNE) and |dy| < |dx| to SmoothFollowApplyENE (ENE).
SmoothFollowTickTargetNorthWest: dx < 0, dy < 0 (north-west): negate dy; |dy| >= |dx| jumps to SmoothFollowApplyNNW (NNW), otherwise SmoothFollowTickGoWNW.
SmoothFollowTickTargetWest: dx < 0 (target west): negate dx, recompute dy, then split into SW (dy >= 0) and NW (SmoothFollowTickTargetNorthWest).
SmoothFollowWriteParentPos: Copy the tick's X/Y to the actor in its $04 prev-link (the spawner, i.e. the visible projectile) and return (RTL). This is the only way the body moves.
SnapToGrid: COP #43 with no operands. If the actor is not 16×16 tile-aligned ((X−8)|Y & $0F ≠ 0), saves snapResumePtr/$7F101A and yields RTI into EnemyPositionSnap; otherwise continues immediately.
SpawnAfter: COP #9B with one Address operand. Calls AllocateActorAfter (list insert + CopyActorState), then sets the new actor script entry pointer from the operand.
SpawnAfterAbs: COP #9F with one Address plus two word operands (absolute X/Y), no users. Spawns after the current actor and assigns $0014/$0016 directly from the operand words.
SpawnAfterAbsFlags: COP #A0 with one Address, two words (X/Y), and one word (flags). SpawnAfterAbs with status flags written to $0010.
SpawnAfterAbsMarked: COP #A3 with one Address, two words (X/Y), and one word (flags). SpawnAfterAbsFlags plus $0040 flag and MarkChildActor.
SpawnAfterFlags: COP #9C with one Address plus one word operand. SpawnAfter plus an initial status-flags word written to $0010.
SpawnAfterMarked: COP #A2 with one Address plus one word (flags). SpawnAfterFlags variant that sets spawner flag $0040 and calls MarkChildActor for parent–child lifecycle tracking.
SpawnAfterOffset: COP #9D with one Address plus two word operands (X/Y offset), no users. Spawns after the current actor and adds the 16-bit offset words to the new actor's $0014/$0016.
SpawnAfterOffsetFlags: COP #9E with one Address, two word offsets, and one word (flags). SpawnAfterOffset with an additional status-flags word stored in $0010.
SpawnAfterOffsetMarked: COP #A4 with one Address, two signed bytes (X/Y offset), and one word (flags). Spawns after current actor with sign-extended byte offsets added to $0014/$0016, sets flags, ORs $0040, and calls MarkChildActor.
SpawnBefore: COP #99 with one Address operand (word+bank entry pointer). Calls AllocateActorBefore (which inserts a list slot and CopyActorState from the spawner), then writes the script entry address to the new actor $0000/$0002.
SpawnBeforeFlags: COP #9A with one Address plus one word operand. Same as SpawnBefore, additionally writing the word operand to the spawned actor status flags ($0010).
SpawnBeforeMarked: COP #A1 with one Address plus one word (flags). SpawnBeforeFlags variant that also ORs $0040 into the spawner flags ($12) and calls MarkChildActor to link parent and child.
SpawnDamageNumberEffect: Entry of the child actor created by SpawnListAppend. $24 = victim slot, $28 = packed BCD damage (written by the caller after the spawn), $14/$16 = victim position at spawn.
SpawnDebrisBurst: Burst actor: LoopStart #08, then per pass WaitByte #03, SpawnAfterFlags DebrisBurstParticle with $10 = $0302, LoopEnd (yields while the counter is nonzero); after the eighth pass it dies. One particle every 5 frames (4 wait + 1 LoopEnd yield).
SpawnDropByHpTier: Drop type 3 (any other nonzero stat byte): same setup, then chooses the body from drop_threshold_by_hp by HP tier and a random byte, and jumps to it with the RTS trick (PLX, PHA, RTS).
SpawnDropGem1: Drop type 1 (stat byte +3 = 1): the 1-gem pickup. Stages the enemy sprite sheet (palette 0) and the marked child collect_handler_gem, then continues in DropBodyGem1.
SpawnDropGem2: Drop type 2 (stat byte +3 = 2): same setup as SpawnDropGem1, then continues in DropBodyGem2 (item $84, 2 gems).
SpawnFieldRevealEffect: Main actor of the reveal: rise, fly to the centre of the event-block rectangle, flash, ten scatter sparkles, background swap, Die. See the block note.
SpawnImpactSparkAndDie: Default victim script and spark spawner: spawn ImpactSparkEffect at this actor (offsets 0, 0, flags $0302) and Die. See the block note for how an actor ends up here.
SpawnItemSparkleEffect: Child actor entry: 8 frames at the spawn position, then 16 frames moving up one pixel per frame, calling AppendSparkleOamEntries each frame.
SpawnListAppend: COP #A5 with one Address, two signed bytes (X/Y offset), and one word (flags). Uses ActorPoolAllocator and appends the new slot at the actor-list tail ($0058), CopyActorState, then applies entry pointer, signed offsets, and flags. On pool exhaustion (carry set) skips all operands without spawning.
SpawnListAppendSpr: COP #A6 with one Address, one byte (animation index), two signed bytes (X/Y offset) and one word (flags), no users. Like SpawnListAppend but also stores the animation index in the spawned actor's $0028; the pool-exhaustion path skips one more operand byte (8 operand bytes in total).
SpawnThinker: COP #3C with one Address operand. Same as SpawnThinkerParam but skips the param byte; allocates a special thinker actor and sets its entry pointer from the script operand.
SpawnThinkerParam: COP #3B with one byte (init param) plus one Address (entry pointer). Allocates a special actor via AllocateSpecialActor, stores param in animScratch+2, writes the far entry pointer to $0000/$0002, copies caller animScratch2, and clears $000E.
speed_zone_ew_fast:
Invisible east–west fast-movement zone actor used in Kress Maze and Mountain Temple.

Uses the same 16×16 proximity test as speed_zone_ew_slow but writes $0007 (+7) to playerSpeedEw when the player is inside the zone. Paired with speed_zone_ew_slow and speed_zone_ns_slow to create directional current lanes.
speed_zone_ew_slow:
Invisible east–west slow-movement zone actor placed in Mountain Temple and related scenes.

When the player center lies within a 16×16 pixel box around the actor, writes $FFF9 (−7) to global playerSpeedEw ($09B4). Returns immediately if the player is outside the zone.
speed_zone_ns_slow:
Invisible north–south slow-movement zone actor with a tighter vertical window than the east–west variants.

Requires the player to be within 16 pixels horizontally and within 4 pixels vertically of the actor center, then sets playerSpeedNs to $FFF9 (−7). Placed in Mountain Temple scenes alongside the EW zones.
SpiralStep: COP #6D with two signed byte operands (diameter delta, angle delta). Adds them to orbitDiameter and orbitAngle, then calls ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef with Y = the reference actor read from the global scratch $0000, which the calling script must set first (mu67_vampires does LDA $24 / STA $0000). The actor is placed at the reference actor's position plus the angle/diameter offset.
StageBgChange: COP #32 with one byte operand: an event-block index. Calls event_blocks.LookupEventBlock, which matches the entry against sceneCurrent and loads its source/destination tile rectangles into the event-block work variables; nothing is drawn yet (the paired ApplyBgChange animates it). LookupEventBlock's carry result (set = no entry for this scene) is ignored.
StageBgChangeFromDeathIdx: COP #34 with no operands. Uses the actor's deathActionIdx ($7F0024, the event-block byte of its scene record) as the event-block index, queues SFX $0F on both sound channels, then jumps into StageBgChange's LookupEventBlock tail to stage the swap. Only SpawnFieldRevealEffect uses it.
StageMove:
COP #52 with three byte operands (animation index, speed, duration cap). Computes absolute distances from moveXAlt/moveYAlt vs the current position, records the sign bits in animScratch2 (bit 14 = X negative, bit 15 = Y negative), halves both distances while the larger exceeds one byte (counting passes in chatPtr), divides the larger distance by |speed| for the frame count (+1, ORed into animScratch2) and initializes TickMove state before the RTI continuation.

Speed ≥ $80 is negated and also adds one halving pass (see the file note). The third operand goes to animScratch+3 and is $FF in all 32 uses; TickMove skips its countdown when bit 7 is set, so $FF means no cap.
StageMoveX: COP #AA with one byte operand (X movement index). Stores it in moveXAlt and puts the X delta chain pointer for that index (AnimFrameLookup into move_chain_table) in actor field $2C.
StageMoveXY: COP #AC with two byte operands (X index, Y index). Does StageMoveX then StageMoveY: stores moveXAlt/moveYAlt and loads the delta chain pointers into $2C and $2E.
StageMoveY: COP #AB with one byte operand (Y movement index). Stores it in moveYAlt and puts the Y delta chain pointer for that index in actor field $2E.
StagePlayerMoveX: COP #90 (copdef StagePlayerMoveX) with two byte operands: animation index and an X movement index. Same staging as StagePlayerSprite; the movement index is kept in moveXAlt ($7F0018) and AnimFrameLookup turns it into the X delta-chain head stored in $2C. 2 sites.
StagePlayerMoveXY: COP #92 (copdef StagePlayerMoveXY) with three byte operands: animation index, X movement index, Y movement index; delta-chain heads go to $2C and $2E. 9 sites.
StagePlayerMoveY: COP #91 (copdef StagePlayerMoveY) with two byte operands: animation index and a Y movement index; the Y delta-chain head goes to $2E, the index to moveYAlt ($7F001A). 21 sites.
StagePlayerSprFromDP: COP #95 with no operands. The animation index is the low byte of the actor's $00 word, which the forced_walk helpers ReadDirSprite_XVelocity/YVelocity store there before the op; afterwards the handler overwrites $00 with the next-op address like StagePlayerSprite. 8 sites, all in forced_walk.
StagePlayerSprite: COP #8F with one byte operand (animation index). Stores it raw in $28, clears $2A, applies the characterForm body with SetActorBody, then saves the next-op address in $00 and the bank in $02. 93 sites.
StagePlayerSprWall: COP #94 with four byte operands (animation index, X movement index, Y movement index, wall type). Same as StagePlayerMoveXY plus a fourth byte stored in playerWallType ($09B0) for the WallAnim ops. No script sites.
StageSprAndHitbox: COP #8D with one byte operand (animation index, 229 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, then UpdateActorAnimation immediately (without yielding) so the first frame's sprite, extents and collision box are set at once, then $2A is cleared again so the animation starts at frame 0 when played. Saves the entry point and continues with RTI.
StageSpriteFrame: COP #80 with one byte operand (animation index, 1200 sites). ProcessAnimFlag sets $28 (and the horizontal flip) and clears $2A; then the entry point ($00) and bank ($02) are set from the next op and the script continues with RTI. The animation is played by a following Anim* op.
StageSpriteLoop: COP #84 with two byte operands (animation index, repeat count; 455 sites). ProcessAnimFlag and sprTimer = the count, the number of complete passes AnimLoop makes (a count of 0 would give 65,536 passes). No movement is staged.
StageSpriteLoopMoveX: COP #85 with three byte operands (animation index, repeat count, X movement index; 278 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, sprTimer = count, moveXAlt = index and $2C = the X delta-chain head.
StageSpriteLoopMoveXY: COP #87 with four byte operands (animation index, repeat count, X movement index, Y movement index; 61 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, sprTimer = count, both indices stored and both delta-chain heads loaded into $2C/$2E.
StageSpriteLoopMoveY: COP #86 with three byte operands (animation index, repeat count, Y movement index; 252 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, sprTimer = count, moveYAlt = index and $2E = the Y delta-chain head.
StageSpriteMoveX: COP #81 with two byte operands (animation index, X movement index; 310 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, then moveXAlt = the index and $2C = move_chain_table[index × 2], the head of the X delta chain (AnimFrameLookup returns a chain pointer, not a duration). Saves the entry point and continues with RTI.
StageSpriteMoveXY: COP #83 with three byte operands (animation index, X movement index, Y movement index; 68 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, then both chains as in StageSpriteMoveX/Y: moveXAlt/moveYAlt hold the indices, $2C/$2E the delta-chain heads.
StageSpriteMoveY: COP #82 with two byte operands (animation index, Y movement index; 331 sites). ProcessAnimFlag, then moveYAlt = the index and $2E = the head of the Y delta chain from move_chain_table. Saves the entry point and continues with RTI.
StageWorldMapChoice: COP #66 with two word operands (start X, Y in pixels) plus one byte (selection ID, 1–$1B in overworld_exit). Writes worldMapStagedX ($0D52), worldMapPlayerY ($0D56) and worldMapChoiceId ($0D58); WorldMapController dispatches a nonzero choice ID through world_map_options. Does not warp immediately.
StageWorldMapMove: COP #65 with two word and two byte operands: world-map start X, start Y (pixels), a byte stored to $0D5E (0 in every shipped script; no reader found), and a route ID stored to worldMapRouteId ($0D5A, index into world_map_route_table). Clears worldMapChoiceId so the route plays directly instead of opening a selection. Does not warp immediately. Used by NPC scripts in Dao, Itory, Watermia, Freejia, Edward Castle, Euro, Nazca, Native Village, South Cape and Angel Village.
StageWorldMapMoveIds: COP #67 with two byte operands: a byte stored to $0D5E (always 0 in shipped scripts; no reader found) and a route ID stored to worldMapRouteId ($0D5A). Used by the world_map_options handlers after the player picks a destination.
StandardEnemyDefeatHandler: Entry (X = the defeated actor). A statsPtr equal to the first enemy_stats_table entry (EnemyInitBasic enemies) jumps to EnemyDefeatFlashAndDrop without counting; so does a boss bit ($0080) in extendedFlags. Otherwise it counts the kill in decimal ($0AEE) and in hex ($0AEC, also stored in orbitAngle: remaining enemies, 0 = last) and falls into EnemyDefeatFlashAndDrop.
StartMusic: COP #04 with one byte operand (music bundle ID). Allocates a thinker with AllocateActorAfter, sets its entry to SpcTransferMusicData, ORs $1000 into its $12 and clears $1000 in its $10 (the mask is $EFFF; it is not the $0800 render bit), and stores the music ID in chatPtr. The thinker runs the SPC handshake and upload asynchronously.
statue_reward_table: Statue table: flag index, sprite (animation index), match value and one tail byte per entry. Read by this actor and inventory_statue_slot (index x 4).
StatueRewardAlreadyClaimed: This statue was collected before the ceremony started: reached by JMP with X = table byte offset and the actor slot on the stack. Sets the frame, shows the statue and idles.
StatueRewardConfettiBurst: One short effect at the statue: X within -8..+7 px, Y 8 px up, frame #02 played once. It runs only when frameCounter AND 3 = 0 on its first tick; otherwise it dies immediately.
StatueRewardEntry: Actor entry (flow steps 1 and 2 of the block note): joypadMaskStd |= $FFFC (every button hidden), NudgePosition (8, 8), metasprite and flags setup, then the direct screen register writes.
StatueRewardNotThisStatue: A statue that is not the one being awarded (match byte differs from globalScriptIndex, and its own flag is still clear): restores X and idles hidden.
StatueRewardOrbitalSparkle: Sparkle that spirals in toward the statue. Start diameter $FC, start angle = the value the ceremony wrote into its $26. Each tick: position = the ceremony actor + orbit(angle, diameter) (ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef), angle + 4, diameter - 2; the actor dies once the diameter is 0 (about 126 ticks).
StopPlayerOnDeath: Zero playerSpeedEw, playerSpeedNs and the actor's $08, then set $0200 in the actor's $10 and return. In: Y = player actor address, 16-bit A.
StrIncreaseStore: Store point of e_str_increase: STR := the new value (the BVC skips the $0255 clamp unless the sum overflowed), print 'Your STR (Strength) has increased!' and Die.
SwitchCase: COP #D9 with two word operands: a low-WRAM address holding the switch variable, and the base (in the script bank) of a table of word script addresses. Reads the byte at the WRAM address, doubles it, fetches the word at base + 2×value (DBR temporarily set to the script bank cached in $0C) and makes it the new script address. There is no range check — a value past the end of the table reads whatever follows it. The doubled index is kept in scratch word $0000, so a script that uses $0000 itself as the variable has it overwritten.
SyncActorPosFromDP: Copies the actor's pixel position (DP $14 / $16) to the home words $7F0010 / $7F0012. Called once by each NPC's init; the wander never moves more than $30 pixels from this point.
SyncPlayerToCamera: Copy this actor's final state to the player actor: position ($14/$16), animation index ($28), $10 with $0008 set (collision-aware movement) and $0200 cleared, and zero the player's $08.
SystemInit:
Full system boot sequence and main game loop.

Boot phase:
1. Native 65816 mode, 16-bit registers
2. Direct page $0000, stack $01FF, data bank $81
3. MEMSEL = 1 (but InitHardwareRegisters writes MEMSEL = 0 afterwards: boot stays SlowROM until sFB_boot_logo enables FastROM)
4. InitHardwareRegisters, InitSystemVariables, SpcLoadBuiltinEngine, EnterForcedBlank (the display stays off until the first scene transition)
5. Sets worldReadyFlag bit 7 (permits scene loading)
6. Reads the byte at $000100 and compares it with $83, but both outcomes leave Y = 0, so sceneNext = 0 for the first ExecuteSceneTransition: no scene is selected. No writer of $83 at $0100 was found (dialog_string_scanner uses $0100 as scratch).
7. Gameplay defaults: max speed 9 per axis, HP 8/8, Str 1, Def 0, slope curve pointers, the six hieroglyph plate slots ($0B28-$0B32) = $FFFF, abilityBitmask = 0
8. sceneNext = $FB (the boot-logo scene, sFB_boot_logo, which hands over to the title screen $FC), then falls into the main loop

Main loop (infinite):
1. VBlankWaitAndJoypad, DisableNmiKeepJoypad
2. General thinkers, scene transition check, warp/chest check, global input, UpdateFrameCounters
3. RunActors_Normal, OAM terminator, depth sort, combat/interaction collision, death check, dodge callbacks
4. CameraSmoothScroll for layer 0 (BG1), then layer 1 (BG2)
5. ResetHdmaState, HDMA-phase thinkers, ComposeAllSprites, UpdateHUD
6. LoadMusicFromTransitionState (blocking SPC upload when a track ID is staged)
7. EnableNmiAndJoypad and loop
TestEventFlag: Core JSR routine that tests one bit in the eventFlags ($0A00) bitfield. ANDs the bitmasks_bit_position entry against the eventFlags byte, then uses SEC/BNE/CLC to return carry set if the bit is set, carry clear if clear. Called by BranchOnFlag, WaitOnFlag COP handlers and all TestFlag JSL wrappers.
TestEventFlag_0200: JSL helper that tests an event flag at base $0200 (persistent world events). Masks to byte, adds $0200, and calls TestEventFlag. Returns carry set if set.
TestFlag_0100: JSL helper that tests event/trigger flag $0100 + (A AND $FF), bytes $0A20–$0A3F (callers include StandardEnemyDefeatHandler, EnemyDefeatDispatch, wall walker, mystic ball and the pyramid Dark Space portal).
TestFlag_0300: JSL helper that tests event flag $0300 + (A AND $FF), bytes $0A60–$0A7F. Most callers pass a scene ID: the flag means this scene's clear reward was already claimed.
TestFlag_0510: JSL helper that tests event flag $0510 + (A AND $FF). inventory_menu's TestAbilityFlag is the only caller: index = characterForm×4 + slot, so these are the ability unlock flags.
TestFlagRaw: JSL helper that tests an event flag without adding a base offset. Masks to byte and calls TestEventFlag directly.
TestWramFlag: Core JSR routine that tests one bit in the wramFlags ($0A80) bitfield. Uses the same byte/bit decomposition as SetWramFlag, ANDs the bit mask against the wramFlags byte, and returns carry set if the flag is set, carry clear otherwise.
TestWramFlag_Offset100:
JSL helper (not COP-dispatched) that tests wramFlags bit $0100 + (A AND 7) and returns carry set when the flag is set.

Index $0100–$0107 gives byte index $20, so it reads $0A80 + $20 = $0AA0 (event flags $0500–$0507) — outside the $20-byte block that ClearAllWramFlags clears. Callers: boss_clear_reward_handler and the boss lair scripts (castoth, sand fanger, vampires, mummy queen, viper) to check a boss's reward/defeat flag.
TickGravity: COP #64 with no operands. Increments the tick counter t and sets the Y delta moveScratch2 = ((t × (t >> 1)) >> f) − v0 using the hardware multiplier (positive = down; v0 is never updated, the curve is recomputed from t each call). RTI returns A = $FFFF once the delta is not negative, the actor's Y is not negative and Y has moved past the target in moveYAlt; otherwise A = $0000.
TickMove: COP #53 with no operands. Per-frame companion to StageMove: MovementVelocityCompute uses hardware multiply/divide to advance position on both axes, waits on UpdateActorAnimation when needed, and yields RTL until the staged trajectory (and any halving passes) completes.
TickMoveComplete: End-of-pass handler for TickMove. Checks chatPtr for remaining halving passes: if non-zero, decrements it, zeroes animScratch and tick counter $24, and jumps back to TickMoveStep for another interpolation pass at halved scale. When chatPtr reaches zero, saves the script PC to $00 and yields RTL to resume the calling script.
TickSineHdma: COP #60 with one byte (delay) and one byte (camera offset). Counts down animScratch+2; on underflow it reloads the delay from the first operand and adds 1 to the sine phase (retPtr1), so the phase advances once every delay + 1 calls. Then reads the second operand as a byte offset into the camera scroll words (cameraTargetX/Y + offset; #02 in every observed call; bit 7 set masks the offset to its low nibble) and rebuilds the HDMA data with BuildSineHdmaTable.
TileAlignCoord:
Packs a pixel coordinate into (page << 8 | tile).

In 8-bit accumulator mode LSR ×4 shifts only the low byte (÷ 16, the tile index within a 256-px page); the hidden high byte (the page) is untouched. After returning to 16-bit mode, AND #$0F0F keeps the low nibble of each byte, and the result is transferred to Y for the caller to store.
TileAlignPosition:
Applies TileAlignCoord to both position parameters.

Subtracts 8 px from X ($14) before packing; Y ($16) is packed as is. The packed words are stored back to $14/$16, where ComputeScrollDeltas uses them as the multiplier (low byte) and divisor (high byte) for MulDivide.
TileCollisionQuery: Internal JSR helper that probes one tile of the $7FC000 collision layer. The probe pixel (WRAM $0018 = X, $001C = Y) must lie inside the camera bounds rectangle (cameraOffsetX/Y up to cameraBoundsX/cameraLowerYBound, X masked to a 16-pixel boundary); it is converted to tile coordinates (Y reduced by one more row), mapped with CalcTileMapOffset, and the collision byte is read through [$80],Y. Returns in A: $000F when the probe is negative or outside the bounds, the map index is ≥ $4000, or the tile's high nibble is non-zero; otherwise the 16-bit word at that index (low byte = the tile's terrain type 0–$F, high byte = the next collision byte, which callers ignore). Called by every BranchIfSolid/BranchIfType handler and the WallAnim handlers.
TileQueryGate: Carry clear (proceed) when $0902 is zero, i.e. the previous 2x2 update has been flushed by the NMI. Otherwise rewinds the script pointer by 2 (back to the COP opcode, so the op runs again next time) and returns carry set; the callers then pop their return and yield.
ToggleHMirror: COP #B8 with no operands. EORs bit $4000 on OAM attribute word $0E to flip horizontal mirroring.
ToggleVMirror: COP #B9 with no operands. EORs bit $8000 on OAM attribute word $0E to flip vertical mirroring.
TownDoorHoldUpLoop: Hold-Up loop: LoopStart sets a counter of 8, BranchIfPressed tests Up ($0800) every frame. Up not held: the count is lost (JumpNextFrame back to the proximity check, which re-enters here with a fresh counter). Up held for 8 consecutive frames: continue at TownDoorOpenSound.
TownDoorInit: Door initialisation: closed frame #01, solid mark, start open if the player is already next to the door, then WaitWhileOffscreen (the loop head of later frames) and TownDoorProximityCheck.
TownDoorOpenIdle: Open state: clear the solid mark, show the open frame #00 and idle on a bare RTL for the rest of the scene visit (nothing closes the door). Also the target when the player is already near at spawn.
TownDoorOpenSound: LoopEnd (counts the held frame; after the 8th it falls through) and the door SFX #0E; falls into TownDoorOpenIdle where the frame actually changes.
TownDoorProximityCheck: Per-frame test: player within 16 px on both axes -> TownDoorHoldUpLoop, otherwise end this pass (the entry pointer stays on WaitWhileOffscreen).
UnlinkActor:
Internal JSR helper that removes the actor at X from the scene's doubly-linked list ($04 previous, $06 next).

Patches the neighbours and the head/tail pointers at $56/$58, then calls ReturnActorSlot. Must be entered with D = X: ReturnActorSlot zeroes D and then sets D = X again. Callers: Die and MarkDeath (the actor itself), KillPrev and KillNext (they switch D and X to the victim first). Removing a sole list entry leaves actorListLast ($58) stale.
UnlinkChildrenCascade: Entry of the child-removal cascade (X = dying actor, reached when actor flag $0040 is set): walks the doubly-linked actor list backward and forward from the dying actor while parentId matches it, returns every slot in that span to the pool with ReturnActorSlot, and patches the list links around the removed span.
UnlockPlayerAfterClimb: End of a glide, standing in for RunAttackCleanup (which the interrupted slide never reaches): zeroes climbStateData ($09E0, the ability damage bonus), clears the consumption bits from joypadMaskStd, sets $10 bit $0008 and clears $0200, consumes the attack press in joypadHeld, clears playerFlags $0002, then RestorePlayerControl.
UpdateFrameCounters:
Per-frame timer maintenance subroutine (called via JSR from main loop).

Decrements the invincibility timer if it's non-negative (bit 15 clear = active). Increments the global frame timer, capping it at $0100 to prevent overflow. Both operations use 16-bit mode.
UpdateFrameDialogue:
Lightweight frame update called during dialogue and text display.

Saves and restores the full register context (B, A, X, Y, D) so it can be called re-entrantly from COP script handlers. Runs RunActors_CutsceneOnly, the OAM terminator, depth sort, camera scroll for both layers, ResetHdmaState, the light HDMA-phase thinkers and sprite composition, then clears displayModeFlags bit 3 (player-tile DMA pending) so the NMI of this frame does the normal VRAM path, waits for VBlank and runs the light general thinkers. It skips the full actor AI pass and the warp/chest checks of the main loop.
UpdateFrameFull:
Complete single-frame update run from inside the NMI handler while the main loop is blocked in a music upload.

NmiHandler calls it when musicTransitionState is positive, i.e. while LoadMusicFromTransitionState is running SpcBlockTransfer with NMI enabled. Runs the light general thinkers, RunActors_OverlayOnly, the OAM terminator, depth sort, camera scroll for both layers, ResetHdmaState, the light HDMA-phase thinkers and sprite composition, between DisableNmiKeepJoypad/VBlankPartial and EnableNmiAndJoypad, so the screen keeps animating during the transfer.
UpdateFrameRender:
Minimal frame update for render-only contexts such as menus and screen transitions.

Saves the full register context. Runs only SortActorsByDepth, ComposeAllSprites, ResetHdmaState, the light HDMA-phase thinkers, UpdateHUD, the VBlank sync and the light general thinkers. Does not run actor AI, camera scrolling or the OAM terminator; the caller is expected to have handled those.
UpdateHUD:
Manages the in-game heads-up display for HP, gems and enemy health.

Returns at once if $09ED bit 6 (HUD off) is set. displayModeFlags bit 0 (full BG3 upload request) is saved on entry and restored on exit, so the BG3 redraw scripts below do not leave a full upload pending; the HUD uses the partial upload (bit 4) instead.

HP recovery animation:
- Skipped when playerStateByte bit 1 (game over, playerFlags bit 9) is set, off an 8-frame boundary, or when hpToHeal is 0
- Decrements hpToHeal and increments playerHp (the displayed HP) toward playerMaxHp, playing sound $0D on each tick; stops when HP equals max HP

Stat display update:
- Compares HP, max HP and gem count with the cached previous values
- On any change: sets displayModeFlags bit 4 (partial BG3 upload), counts the hundreds digit of the gem count by repeated subtraction of 100, and redraws the counters with a BG3 console script

Enemy health bar:
- When enemyHpPending is nonzero: draws the bar and sets enemyHealthTimer to 60 (the $19 stored first is overwritten)
- Otherwise the timer counts down; at 0 the displayed enemy HP is cleared and the bar redrawn at once (the $1E stored first is overwritten by the STZ, so there is no separate fadeout phase)

Finally caches HP, max HP and gems for the next frame's change detection and restores displayModeFlags bit 0.
UpdateHUD_Active: Body of UpdateHUD, entered when hudDisableFlag bit 6 (HUD off) is clear: it saves displayModeFlags bit 0 and runs the HP recovery animation, the stat-change redraw, the enemy health bar timer and the cache update described in the UpdateHUD note.
UploadScrollRegisters:
Writes BG1 and BG2 scroll positions to PPU hardware registers.

Two modes based on scrollModeFlags bit 3:
- Normal mode: Uses WriteBgScroll with indexed layer data. Respects layerPriorityFlag — when negative, swaps the order BG1/BG2 are written to handle layer priority changes.
- Direct mode (bit 3 set): Writes bg1ScrollH/mapScrollV directly to BG1HOFS/BG1VOFS registers, masking high bytes to 7 bits.
WaitByte:
COP $DA with a 1-byte operand (frame count): sleep the actor for N+1 ticks, then resume after the operand.

Reads the count (the 16-bit read also pulls in the next script byte, hence the AND), then falls into the shared tail WaitStoreAndYield, which stores it in waitCounter ($08), saves the resume address to entryPtr ($00/$02) and yields by discarding the COP stack frame and returning with RTL to the actor loop.
WaitForAnimFrame: COP #8C with one byte operand (target frame index; 29 sites). Calls UpdateActorAnimation and yields until the frame counter $2A equals the operand. $2A is read after UpdateActorAnimation already incremented it, so the script resumes one stage earlier than a literal reading suggests: when frame operand − 1 has just been staged. If the list ends first the movement chains are cleared and the script continues; the operand is consumed on every path.
WaitForButton: COP #3E blocking input wait taking one word operand: a button mask (bit 0 selects joypadRaw instead of joypadCurrent, see the block note). Yields via RTL, re-running the op every frame, until any masked button is down. No vanilla extracted script uses it (the dialogue renderer has its own wait command, DialogCmd_WaitForButton); only the dispatch table references it.
WaitForRelease: COP #3F with one word operand (button mask, bit 0 selects joypadRaw instead of joypadCurrent). Yields via RTL (rewinding the script PC) until none of the masked buttons is down, then advances with RTI. With bit 0 clear a consumed or masked button already counts as released.
WaitOnFlagByte: COP #D2 with one byte (flag) and one byte (sense). Saves a rewind entry PC, then yields RTL each frame until TestEventFlag matches the requested sense (set or clear).
WaitOnFlagWord: COP #D3 with one word (flag) and one byte (sense). Word-indexed variant of WaitOnFlagByte with the same yield-until-match behavior.
WaitStoreAndYield: Shared tail of WaitByte and WaitWord (A = frame count): stores the count in waitCounter ($08), copies the resume bank and PC from the COP frame ($0C/$0A) into the entry pointer ($02/$00), then discards the COP stack frame with two PLA and returns with RTL to the actor loop, which resumes the actor when the counter goes negative.
WaitWhileOffscreen: COP #27 with one byte operand (delay count n). If actor flag $4000 is set in $10 (off-screen), sets the entry ($00) to this COP instruction (PC − 2), stores n in $08 and yields, so the test repeats n + 1 ticks later (the WaitByte rule); otherwise it skips the operand and continues.
WaitWord:
COP $DB with a 2-byte operand (frame count): same wait as WaitByte for delays over 255 ticks.

Reads the 16-bit count and branches into WaitByte's shared tail (WaitStoreAndYield).
WallAnimHere: COP #96 with one word operand (joypad mask, compared for equality with joypadCurrent). If the masks differ the op continues at once. If Y is 16-aligned it probes the tile at the actor; a block (TileCollisionQuery returned $000F) sets actor flag $0004 and continues; a tile type different from playerWallType continues without animating; otherwise (or when Y is not aligned) it runs UpdateActorAnimation and yields until the animation finishes. No script sites.
WallAnimNorth: COP #97, same as WallAnimHere but the probe pixel is Y - $10. No script sites.
WallAnimSouth: COP #98, same as WallAnimHere but the probe pixel is Y + $10. No script sites.
WriteApuIo0: COP #0A with one byte operand. Writes the byte directly to APU I/O port APUIO0 ($2140) for SPC700 communication.
WriteApuIo1: COP #09 with one byte operand. Writes the byte directly to APU I/O port APUIO1 ($2141) for SPC700 communication.
WriteBgScroll:
Writes horizontal and vertical scroll values for one background layer.

X index selects the scroll data source (0=BG1, 2=BG2). Y index selects the PPU register target.

For each axis (H and V), checks an override flag at $06C7+X / $06CB+X:
- If negative (bit 7 set): uses the scroll override value instead of normal scroll
- If positive: uses the standard scroll position

High bytes are masked to 2 bits (10-bit scroll position for Mode 1 backgrounds).
